skill.name: to-issues
skill.description: Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable issues on the project issue tracker using tracer-bullet vertical slices.
skill.summary: Turns plans and PRDs into sequenced issue tracker work.

content.value_statement: Large plans are hard to divide into issues that agents can complete independently. This skill turns plans, specs, and PRDs into approved vertical slices for an issue tracker.
actual_capabilities: Breaks plans, specs, and PRDs into narrow vertical slices.
Reviews slice granularity and dependency order with the user before publishing.
Formats issue bodies with parent, build scope, acceptance criteria, and blockers.
Supports wide refactors by sequencing expand, migrate, and contract work.
Publishes approved issues in blocker-first order when an issue tracker is available.
limitations: Requires issue tracker context and label vocabulary from the surrounding setup.
Does not define the issue tracker integration itself.
Relies on user approval before creating final issues.
Does not implement the planned work after issues are created.

use_cases.title: Split a Product Spec
use_cases.description: Convert a product spec into independent engineering issues with clear dependencies and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Prepare Agent Work
use_cases.description: Create issue slices that remote coding agents can pick up without needing the full planning discussion.

use_cases.title: Plan a Wide Refactor
use_cases.description: Sequence a broad refactor with expand, migrate, and contract issues that keep integration risk visible.

prompt_templates.title: Break Down This Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a plan already in the chat.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to turn the plan above into independently grabbable issue slices. Show the proposed list before publishing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Use an Existing Issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a tracker issue as the source material.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use issue #123 as the parent source. Read the body and comments, then propose vertical slice issues with blockers and user stories covered.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Slice Size
prompt_templates.scenario: The first breakdown needs review before publishing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed slices for granularity. Merge anything too small, split anything too broad, and keep each issue independently verifiable.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a broad technical migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: This is a wide refactor. Use expand-contract planning instead of tracer bullets, and propose blocker-first issues that keep CI green between batches.

output_examples.input: A PRD for adding team invites, role assignment, and invitation emails.
output: Issue 1 creates the invite request path with validation and audit coverage.
Issue 2 adds role selection and permission checks after the invite path exists.
Issue 3 sends invitation emails and verifies retry behavior.

output_examples.input: A plan to rename a shared API field across a large codebase.
output: First issue adds the new field while keeping the old field working.
Migration issues update callers in dependency-aware batches.
Final issue removes the old field after every caller has moved.

best_practices: Provide the source plan, issue tracker, and label vocabulary before using the skill.
Approve the proposed slice list only after checking dependencies and issue size.
Keep each issue focused on one verifiable end-to-end behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not publish issues before the user approves the proposed breakdown.
Do not create horizontal layer tasks when a vertical slice can deliver value.
Do not inline detailed code snippets that will become stale.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates issue tracker tasks from a plan, spec, PRD, or existing parent issue.

faq.question: Does it publish issues automatically?
faq.answer: It asks the user to review the proposed issue breakdown before publishing approved issues.

faq.question: What is a vertical slice?
faq.answer: A vertical slice is a narrow end-to-end change that can be tested or demonstrated on its own.

faq.question: How does it handle broad refactors?
faq.answer: It uses expand-contract sequencing so the system can stay working while callers migrate.

faq.question: Does it require a specific tracker?
faq.answer: No specific tracker is defined here, but the environment must provide tracker access and label rules.

faq.question: Can it implement the issues?
faq.answer: No. It plans and publishes issues, but implementation is handled by users or other agents.
